edges.effect_quant: The strongest pooled postoperative evidence supports a clinically meaningful pain benefit from levonorgestrel-releasing intrauterine systems in endometriosis. A 2018 meta-analysis of 491 patients found greater pain reduction after surgery (MD 12.97, 95% CI 5.55 to 20.39), while two randomized trials also reported significant improvement in chronic pelvic pain and dysmenorrhea over six months.
edges.population: women with confirmed endometriosis using a levonorgestrel-releasing intrauterine system for postoperative maintenance or pain control
edges.mechanism: Levonorgestrel-releasing intrauterine systems suppress endometrial proliferation, reduce menstrual bleeding, and create a more progestogenic local hormonal environment. In endometriosis, that combination can dampen cyclic inflammatory stimulation of ectopic lesions and reduce dysmenorrhea and chronic pelvic pain.
edges.summary: For endometriosis-associated pelvic pain, the literature leans clearly protective. Randomized comparisons and pooled postoperative analyses suggest LNG-IUS meaningfully improves pelvic pain and dysmenorrhea, although the effect size varies by comparator and the best evidence is strongest for postoperative maintenance rather than every endometriosis phenotype.
edges.caveats: This edge should be interpreted as a treatment-signal for selected patients, not proof that every hormonal IUD works equally well for every endometriosis presentation. Bleeding-pattern changes and comparator choice matter, and some trials show similar improvement to active hormonal alternatives rather than a uniquely superior effect.
